data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The generator is FAIR over 10000 draws: the structural modular bias, while real, is small enough (~1.4 ppm) that the truncated orbit of 10000 draws does not amplify it beyond two standard deviations, and all six counts will fall within [1614, 1720].","counterconditions":[{"case":"The LCG's orbit of 10000 happens to land on a sub-cycle that systematically over-samples residues 0 and 1, pushing count_1 above 1719.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The standard deviation formula used is incorrect and the actual tolerance is tighter.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The implementation reveals that one or more counts fall outside [1614, 1720].","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The modular bias divides the 2^31 states unevenly (two residues get one extra state each), but this is a 1.4e-6 effect per state. Over a short, non-full-period orbit of 10000 draws, the LCG behaves close to a uniform sampler for the purpose of die faces. The expected count for each face is ~1666.67 with standard deviation ~52.7. Even if face 1 is slightly over-represented, the expected excess is small (~0.002 expected over 10000 draws from the pure modular bias alone). The actual count will be dominated by the LCG's pseudo-random fluctuations, which, for this common LCG, are known to be reasonable for short horizons. Thus all counts fall within [1666.67 - 105.4, 1666.67 + 105.4] = [1561, 1772], which easily contains the [1614, 1720] window predicted by the tolerance.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
